Event Tickets–specific listing copy — what translates differently

Concert, sports, theater, and show event ticket listings use vocabulary general Wallet guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe live event entry passes — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Event Tickets vs Add Event Tickets to Wallet vs 演出票 vs 活动门票

US pages use "Event Tickets", "Add Event Tickets to Wallet", or "Your concert tickets in Apple Wallet." China storefront copy often uses 演出票 for concert and theater frames and 活动门票 when your English frames emphasize general live-event entry. Apple keeps Event Tickets as a product term where appropriate alongside Chinese phrasing on screenshot overlays. Do not use 登机牌 — that signals airline boarding pass marketing, not event ticket entry.

Venue & 场馆

Gallery frames show venue name rows on the event ticket card — "Madison Square Garden" or arena callouts. Chinese buyers expect 场馆 on venue rows — distinct from hotel room 开锁 on the Hotel Keys guide and airline gate rows on the Boarding Pass guide.

Section & 座位区

Section and seating-area rows appear on event ticket screenshots — "Section 102" or seating-zone callouts. Chinese App Store copy uses 座位区 when your English frames show section rows — not 登机口 from the Boarding Pass guide or 客房钥匙 from the Hotel Keys guide.

Show date & 场次

Event ticket apps show show date and time rows on pass cards — "Sat, Oct 12 · 8:00 PM" or door-time callouts. Chinese copy uses 场次 when your gallery shows show-date rows — describing the buyer-visible frame your screenshots show, not ticketing backend engineering we do not deliver.

Genre-specific phrasing — 演出门票 & 球赛门票

Concert and theater frames may use 演出门票 when your English source names live performance entry. Sports frames may use 球赛门票 when your gallery shows stadium or arena sports entry. AppLocale picks genre phrasing that matches your English claims — not airline 航班登机牌 or loyalty 会员卡 vocabulary.
